Michael / team —

Thanks again for progressing through the eval. Per our MAP conversation last week, we pulled together a concise final acceptance playbook and the signature matrix for OrbitX to review (attached: MAP_v4.xlsx, signature-matrix.pdf).

Objective: land a clean go/no-go decision, complete signatures, and have a deterministic start-date for onboarding and canary traffic. Quick asks from our side:
- Can Legal confirm if the standard SLA appendix (section 5.2) needs a customer-specific amendment? If so, flag the exact clause by EOD Tue (11 Aug).
- Please confirm signatory availability windows next week (24–26 Aug proposed) or suggest alternatives.
- Confirm preferred production start date (we've penciled in 2026-09-01 for a staged rollout).

I've cc'd Priyom for deployment sequencing and Ben for commercial/DocuSign routing. If we get verbal go by end of next week, we can queue DocuSign and expedite the PO lock.

Attachments: MAP_v4.xlsx (mutual action plan), signature-matrix.pdf (who signs what + windows).

Thanks,
Stephanie

Michael / team —

Operational notes from engineering and deployment sequencing:
- Priyom will own the canary rollout (scope: 0.5% traffic -> 5% -> 25% over two weeks). Priyom: can you confirm the maintenance window preference (UTC evening or PST early morning)?
- If Legal requests SLA language that impacts incident MTTR obligations, we need to confirm whether OrbitX requires on-call warm-handoff (we can provide a 7x24 on-call addendum if needed — this will affect ramp timing).
- Backup plan: if signatures slip past 26 Aug we can still aim for a Sep 7 start but would need to compress the canary (7 days) and increase monitoring thresholds.

I recommend we:
1) Lock DocuSign envelope on Mon 23 Aug (Ben will send).
2) OrbitX confirms signers and any SLA redlines by Thu 13 Aug.
3) Legal + Procurement complete countersign by Tue 25 Aug.

Aditya
